same_vehicle_discipline: Q80's 125 ms GPU and 15.2 GB/s were measured on the Q4 vehicle, so this compares them against the Q4 byte budget (1.8925 GB/token). Mixing a mixed-artifact byte budget with a Q4 runtime is exactly the category error that invalidated G013 v1.
finding: Q80's GPU achieves 15.2 GB/s where a no-model control moving the SAME bytes in the SAME 98-CB, 10-of-512 gather shape achieves 320-411 GB/s. The kernels are 21-27x off a control that is itself already measured on this box, in this access pattern, with no model logic. This is not a bandwidth-ceiling problem and not a density problem.
why_this_outranks_density: Routed experts are 9% of per-token bytes (G013_FS_EFFICIENCY_CLOSURE_V2). Even compressing them to zero removes 9% of traffic. Closing a 21-27x kernel gap is worth an order of magnitude more, and it is the SAME lever for G001, G017 and G020.
caveat: The control is a load-only kernel. Real decode must also compute, so 21-27x is an upper bound on the recoverable factor, not a promise. The honest claim is that the headroom between 15.2 GB/s and 320 GB/s is kernel-shaped, not ceiling-shaped.
